input.brief: Name the late-game orbital ability on Solstice's globe layer: the player calls sunlight down from orbit as a beam that burns Blight off a wide patch of the map. It costs a lot of stored power and can only be used on a long charge. It needs a name for its button and tooltip, one to three words.
input.context: Solstice (formerly RECLAIM) is Isaac's solarpunk RTS for PC, built in Unreal 5.8. The player is a stone guardian (an armored stone golem, working name Gardener) who commands a colony of reclaimed machines and cleansed animals; there are no human settlers. The enemy is the Blight: a dense magenta fog that shelters infected animals and corrupted machines led by Bull commanders. Sunlight burns the Blight, so it attacks at night. A day is a loop: day to build and cleanse (currency Lumen; solar and wind make stored power), dusk as a gamble, night waves held with sun lamps, dawn to repair and unlock. Restored land pushes the fog back; surviving three nights reclaims the region. Look contract: white, brass and cyan against the magenta Blight, lit greenhouses, planters growing on machines. Reference games: They Are Billions, Terra Nil, Halo Wars scale, Deadlock for the character HUD.

input.brief: A tagline for the Solstice promo: the last card of the trailer and the line on the store capsule. At most seven words. It plays to people who already love base-builders and colony games like They Are Billions and Terra Nil.

input.brief: A name for the agent that takes a sound-design brief, searches Isaac's Soundly cloud library (non-Pro sounds by default) and stages the best finds in a temporary collection called Eva picks in his Soundly app so he can audition them. A sibling agent removes that collection a day later. The name is the agent's id in a CLI and in a list of agents, so one word or a short kebab-case phrase.
input.context: The agent lives in atomic-agents, a package of narrow specialist agents named for their job: design-critic, web-researcher, prop-render, diagram, widget, gmail, soundly-cleanup. The current working id is soundly-picks. Isaac scores his games and promo videos with sounds from Soundly, and wants picks to audition quickly, not a finished mix. The agent never downloads or buys anything and does not touch Pro-only sounds unless asked.

input.brief: The headline (H1) of the free demand letter template page at /demand-letter-template on the GoodOps marketing site. The visitor is an office manager or owner at a small pest-control company with a customer who is weeks past due, and who found the page by searching for a demand letter for payment. The page gives them a free letter generator. Headline only, under 12 words.
input.context: GoodOps sells two tools to pest-control companies that run on FieldRoutes (also called PestRoutes): AI Collections for overdue balances ($500 per branch per month, $400 billed yearly) and a white-label customer Mobile App. The demand letter page is free SEO bait that must be useful on its own and earn trust for AI Collections. Today its title tag reads "Demand Letter Template for Payment (Free Generator)". Below the headline the page lists when a demand letter is the right step: reminders went unanswered, a call was tried, the balance is confirmed, you will follow through. Readers are busy, practical and a little uncomfortable about sending a demand to a long-time customer.

input.brief: A visual direction for the Solstice command-view HUD: the build bar (seven build icons with Lumen costs), selected state, tooltips, the Hold and Follow commands, the power and Lumen readouts and the day, dusk, night and dawn clock. It sits over the wide RTS camera, so it must stay readable on a bright green day and on a dark night full of magenta fog. Isaac rejected the old white build shelf and wants a compact icon cluster bottom-left with no panel behind it, the selected icon outlined in cyan and a small tooltip with the build name.

input.brief: A visual direction for the Solstice promo: a 30 to 45 second trailer and its key art. Footage comes from the Unreal build at the wide RTS camera and the close guardian camera, so the direction has to work on in-engine captures plus graphics, type and grading added in post. It should make a viewer who likes colony and base-building games want to wishlist it.
